This mind map organizes every piece of information provided in the article about R. G. LeTourneau.

Central Node: R. G. LeTourneau (Robert Gilmour LeTourneau | 1888–1969)

  • 1. Identity & Overview

    • Roles: Business magnate, Inventor, Philanthropist.
    • Key Designations:
      • "The Dean of Earthmoving."
      • Known for inventing earthmoving and heavy machinery technology.
    • Vital Stats:
      • Born: Nov 30, 1888 (Richford, Vermont).
      • Died: June 1, 1969 (Longview, Texas) at age 80.
      • Family: Spouse Evelyn Peterson (m. 1917); 5 Children (Richard, Roy, Ted, Ben, Louise).
    • Major Impact Statistics:
      • Secured 299 patents.
      • Supplied nearly 75% of earthmoving equipment used by Allied forces in WWII.
      • Equipment built >50% of the 1,500-mile Alaska Highway.

  • 2. Early Life & Education

    • Locations: Born in VT → Moved to Duluth, MN → Moved to Portland, OR.
    • Schooling:
      • Dropped out of high school at age 14.
      • Apprenticeship: Ironworker at East Portland Iron Works (learned foundry & machinist trades).
      • Correspondence Courses:
        • International Correspondence Schools (Mechanical Engineering basics) — did not complete assignments initially.
        • Received diploma in 1965 (age 76), 50 years later.
        • Automobile course (1909) — "Bachelor of Motorcycles" (disassembled/reassembled motorcycle in a day).
    • Early Employment:
      • Jobs: Wood cutter, farm hand, miner, carpenter's laborer.
      • Yerba Buena Power Plant (San Francisco): Learned welding and electricity application.
      • WWI: Refused military service due to permanent neck injuries (racing accident); worked as maintenance assistant at Mare Island Navy Yard (electrical machinist).

  • 3. Business Career

    • The Garage Phase (Stockton, CA):
      • 1909: Moved to Stockton.
      • 1911: Half-owner of Superior Garage ($1,000 stake); potentially first building dedicated to car sales/service in the area.
      • Post-WWI: Garage business failed.
      • The Pivot: Repaired a Holt crawler tractor to pay debts → employed to level 40 acres using tractor + towed scraper.
    • The Contractor Phase (1920–1933):
      • Jan 1920: Purchased used Holt tractor; started land leveling business.
      • May 1921: Established engineering workshop in Stockton to design/build scrapers.
      • Notable Projects: Boulder Highway to Hoover Dam (NV), Marysville Levees, Orange County Dam, Newhall Cut-off (CA).
    • The Manufacturing Empire (R. G. LeTourneau, Inc.):
      • Incorporated: 1929 in California.
      • Expansion:
        • 1935: Plant in Peoria, Illinois.
        • 1938: Plant in Toccoa, Georgia.
        • 1941: Plant in Rydalmere, Australia.
        • 1942: Plant in Vicksburg, Mississippi.
        • 1945: Plant in Longview, Texas.
    • Major Corporate Shifts:
      • 1953 Sale: Sold earth-moving line to Westinghouse Air Brake Company (WABCO) for $31 million.
      • 1958 Re-entry: Started LeTourneau Technologies (age 70) focusing on high-capacity machines & electric wheel drive.
      • 1966 Retirement: Handed leadership to son Richard (age 77) but continued designing daily.
      • Post-LeTourneau Ownership: Sold to Marathon (1970) → Rowan (1986) → Joy Global (2011) → Komatsu Mining Corp.

  • 4. Technical Contributions & Inventions

    • Scrapers: Introduced single-person operated power control units (load, haul, dump, spread).
    • Tires: Replaced wide steel wheels with low-pressure, heavy-duty rubber tires (prevented cutting into sand).
    • Electric Wheel: Diesel-generator powered electric motors placed on each driving wheel (hub motors).
    • Tournapull: Developed the two-wheeled tractor unit.
    • Offshore: Concepts for mobile offshore drilling platforms.
    • Philosophy: Predicted machines would grow from "tons" to "hundreds of tons" capacity and "thousands of horsepower."

  • 5. Faith & Philanthropy

    • Personal Faith:
      • Devout Christian; typically credited God for his success.
      • Financial Model: "God's Businessman" — Set aside 90% of salary/profits for donations; lived on 10%.
      • Quote: "I shovel out the money, and God shovels it back – but God has a bigger shovel."
      • Verse: Matthew 6:33 inscribed on his grave.
    • Ministry Work:
      • Layman leader in Christian & Missionary Alliance, Gideons International, Christian Business Men's Connection (CBMC).
      • Traveled thousands of miles weekly for 30 years to speak.
    • LeTourneau University (Longview, TX):
      • Founded 1946 (originally LeTourneau Technical Institute).
      • Site: Former Harmon General Hospital.
      • Philosophy: Combine practical work, education, and Christian testimony.
      • Status: Became a university in 1961.
    • International Development:
      • Liberia (1953): Colonization, land/ag development, evangelism.
      • Peru (1954): "Tournavista" project with similar goals.

  • 6. Awards & Recognition

    • Industry Awards:
      • 1936: "Appreciation of Service Achievement" (Six Companies Inc, for Boulder Dam).
      • 1956: Frank P. Brown Medal.
      • 1958: "Beavers Award" (Heavy construction industry).
    • Honorary Namesakes:
      • LeTourneau Hall (Toccoa Falls College).
      • Toccoa Airport (R. G. LeTourneau Field).
    • Work Style Legacy: Known for working alongside engineers/employees and preferring the factory floor/drawing board to executive offices.

  • 7. End of Life

    • Event: Suffered severe stroke (March 1969).
    • Death: June 1, 1969.
    • Burial: On the campus of LeTourneau University (alongside wife Evelyn).
